images.caption: Figure 1:From interaction traces to an agent-operated simulated environment.Trace2Env reconstructs traces into a reusable environment worldbook containing schemas, grounded evidence, and induced behavioral knowledge. During simulation, a task agent supplies actions, while a world model agent actively consults the worldbook together with the current episode state and episodic memory to infer their consequences and predict the resulting observations.
Figure 2:Trace2Env framework.Trace2Env reconstructs historical traces into an environment worldbook and uses a world model agent to operate it as a stateful simulated environment.

Figure 4:The task agent generates an unsupportedputaction. Direct Prompting hallucinates a successful placement, causing a false state transition and a simulated success that fails under real-environment replay. Trace2Env not only predicts the correct no-op, but also uses its worldbook and persistent state tracking to preserve the inventory state and support subsequent interaction, enabling recovery with the validmovecommand.
